item.title: Tasmania spent 28 years removing invasive carp from two lakes; after 49,301 fish were...
item.description: After a remarkable 28-year campaign, Tasmania's fisheries service has successfully eliminated invasive common carp from Lake Sorell and Lake Crescent. This effort has seen the removal of over 49,000 harmful fish, leading to clearer waters and the revival of native plant life in marsh areas. The resurgence of wild brown trout has also enhanced recreational fishing opportunities for anglers, proving that large lakes can recover from invasive species.

item.title: In 2002, New Mexico began one of America’s largest native-fish restoration projects...
item.description: A significant conservation initiative has successfully reinstated native trout species across more than 120 miles of streams by eliminating non-native predators and restoring habitats in two states. The reintroduction of the Rio Grande cutthroat trout has led to the establishment of a self-sustaining population, averting the need for federal endangered species status. This successful strategy serves as a blueprint for other western states aiming to restore native fish populations.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: In 2006, Idaho launched a bounty-and-netting war on invasive lake trout; a decade later...
item.description: A vigorous initiative employing commercial nets and angler incentives has successfully diminished the population of invasive lake trout. This management program has fostered a remarkable resurgence of native species such as rainbow trout and sockeye salmon. Hydroacoustic assessments revealed kokanee densities that haven't been observed since the 1970s. The rebound of kokanee has instigated beneficial shifts throughout the broader ecosystem.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: 68-year-old Sheila Consaul bought Ohio lighthouse for $71,010 in 2011, restored it for over $300K
item.description: At 68, Sheila Consaul owns Ohio’s historic Fairport Harbor West Lighthouse, which she bought for $71,010 at auction in 2011. After years of restoration and more than $300,000 in investment, she transformed the abandoned century-old landmark into an off-grid summer home featuring rainwater collection, solar power, historic interiors and stunning views of Lake Erie.

item.title: In 1911, Norwegian whalers released 10 reindeer on South Georgia for food and hunting
item.description: In 1911, reindeer were introduced to South Georgia by Norwegian whalers. This led to significant ecological issues, as the absence of natural predators allowed their numbers to explode, resulting in harm to delicate coastal ecosystems and native species. A comprehensive eradication initiative was launched, successfully culling almost 7,000 reindeer, thereby aiding the natural recuperation of the damaged habitats, with native flora and seabirds starting to reappear.

item.title: Six years after Michigan dam disaster, water returns to Smallwood Lake
item.description: Smallwood Lake in Michigan has started refilling after work on Smallwood Dam reached substantial completion in July. The refill began on August 4 and is expected to take eight to 10 weeks. Meanwhile, work continues at Secord and Edenville dams, with Secord facing a delay after crews found a problem with a spillway gate.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Virgin Australia removed a wheelchair user because his mobility device would not fit under his seat
item.description: Virgin Australia has issued an apology to Shane Hryhorec after he was removed from a flight due to a misunderstanding regarding the safety of his wheelchair's power add-on motor. Despite Hryhorec's explanation that the device easily detaches, airline staff insisted on his removal. This incident unveils the need for improved accessibility training in airlines. In response, Virgin Australia is reassessing staff procedures and offering Hryhorec a full refund.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Both pilots fell asleep as a plane carrying 153 passengers drifted off course
item.description: In a startling incident, two Batik Air pilots dozed off simultaneously for roughly thirty minutes, causing their aircraft to veer off course. Communications from air traffic control went unanswered during this time. Thankfully, the plane landed without any injuries, prompting Indonesian authorities to reassess protocols regarding pilot fatigue and procedures for night operations to ensure safety.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: She got her first dolls' house at 8; now, at 101, she runs a museum
item.description: Val Ripley, aged 101, continues her lifelong fascination with dolls' houses and their historical significance. Her childhood toy, lost during the war, was rediscovered and inspired a museum. This museum showcases miniature homes as documents of social history and changing lifestyles. The collection features dolls' houses dating back to 1840, reflecting evolving domestic life. Val's enduring connection to these tiny worlds spans nearly a century.
item.dc:creator: TOI Lifestyle Desk

item.title: 84-year-old woman found alive in rubble three days after Indonesia quake
item.description: In an inspiring turn of events, an 84-year-old woman named Paulina Pobi was successfully rescued after enduring three harrowing days trapped under rubble in Nitunglea village on Flores island. Against the odds, she survived without sustenance, while rescue teams faced significant obstacles from landslides and damaged infrastructure. This incredible story of survival emerged as a beacon of hope amid the widespread destruction and displacement caused by the earthquake.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Why Pakistan’s donkeys are becoming valuable in China: What is driving this surprising demand
item.description: Pakistani donkeys are increasingly valuable due to rising Chinese demand for ejiao. China's own donkey population struggles to meet the demand for this traditional product. Pakistan has become a key part of this international supply chain after finalizing export protocols. The rising prices of donkeys impact local families who depend on them for livelihoods. This situation highlights the complex intersection of local needs and global trade.
